{ "entries"  

: [ { "name_han"  : "酉阳杂俎" , "logic_thesis"  : "Core argument is that the anomalous is not noise but evidence of patterned qi-response: prodigies, dreams, and local cults prove Heaven–Earth–human correspondence operates through omen-logic rather than pure moral sermon. It establishes a taxonomy of the strange so that causality can be read from irregular events, not only from classics. Thus miscellany becomes a method of induction for cosmotechnical judgment." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: all beings and events are permutations of qi under yin–yang/Five Phases.
2) Premises of experience: anomalies (yao, guai, dreams, crafts, local gods) repeatedly co-occur with human action and seasonal/space conditions.
3) Inference: if co-occurrence is stable, anomalies are readable signs, not random marvels.
4) Inference: classification of the strange yields rules of resonance (ganying) usable beyond court historiography.
5) Conclusion: correct knowledge of fate and ritual requires collecting and sorting liminal cases as data for correspondence reasoning." , "logic_practice"  : "1) In BaZi, treat ‘strange’ chart features (extreme imbalance, void, clash clusters) as omen-data, not discard as noise.
2) Build a personal case-file of life events ↔ pillar combinations to induce personal ganying patterns.
3) When a year/month brings anomalous signs, map them to the chart’s active agents before moralizing.
4) For cultivation, use night dreams and body omens as feedback on qi practice rather than superstition to suppress.
5) Prefer multi-source evidence (calendar + body + locale) over single classic quotation." , "logic_compare"  : "Unlike systematic Daoist canons (e.g. Baopuzi) that argue from doctrine downward, Youyang Zazu argues from curated anomaly upward. Unlike pure zhiguai entertainment, it implies an empirical archive for correspondence. Its edge is inductive classification of the uncanny as a logic tool for reading fate." } , { "name_han"  : "新镌京版工师雕斫正式鲁班经匠家镜" , "logic_thesis"  : "It proves that craft geometry is applied cosmotechnics: correct measure, orientation, and ritual timing convert raw material into a vessel that hosts auspicious qi and repels sha. Carpentry is not mere technique but a micro-ritual of Heaven–Earth alignment. Error in proportion or rite is therefore structural misfortune, not aesthetic failure." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: buildings/tools mediate human dwelling within directional qi fields.
2) Premise: Lu Ban tradition encodes proportions, axes, and taboo days as transmission of cosmic order.
3) Inference: form that matches cosmic measure concentrates shengqi; form that violates it generates sha.
4) Inference: ritual inauguration (offerings, taboo avoidance) seals the geometric work as a living vessel.
5) Conclusion: mastery of craft is inseparable from calendar, direction, and propitiation—technique without rite is incomplete causality." , "logic_practice"  : "1) Align chart ‘structure’ metaphors with house/tool: Day Master as center, supporting stems as load-bearing axes.
2) When advising fengshui/BaZi lifestyle, prioritize orientation and taboo timing over decorative fixes.
3) Treat ‘broken structure’ in BaZi (severe clash/combination damage) as needing reconstruction sequence, not only luck charms.
4) Cultivation analog: regulate body-as-house—breath, posture, schedule—as measured craft under seasonal rules.
5) Use craft-taboo logic for choosing start dates of projects from the natal chart’s useful gods." , "logic_compare"  : "Differs from pure fengshui manuals by rooting spatial logic in artisan process and tool-making, not only landscape form. Differs from philosophical Daoism by proving cosmology through buildable measure. Why: it makes the abstract axis of Heaven–Earth into a workshop protocol." } , { "name_han"  : "天妃显圣录" , "logic_thesis"  : "It argues that maritime salvation by Tianfei is evidence of virtue-power (de) becoming operational force across space: sincere distress plus correct invocation activates a responsive numen. Empire, merchants, and fishers are equalized under one rescue logic—authority of the goddess is proven by repeatable miracle pattern, not by bloodline. Thus cult legitimacy is empirical ganying under crisis." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: the sea is a realm of extreme contingency where human skill is insufficient.
2) Premise: repeated rescues follow prayer, moral sincerity, and recognition of Tianfei’s titles.
3) Inference: efficacy clusters around invocation + de, proving responsive presence.
4) Inference: state and local recognition follow efficacy, so cult grows by verified response, not only decree.
5) Conclusion: the goddess’s ‘logic’ is crisis–sincerity–response; devotion is rational risk-management under cosmically ordered mercy." , "logic_practice"  : "1) In BaZi crisis years (travel, water elements extreme, danger stars), prioritize sincere vow-ritual over fatalist resignation.
2) Map ‘rescue’ deities to chart useful gods: when Water is both danger and resource, cultivate responsive devotion + skill.
3) Practice: short, specific petitions tied to concrete dangers (journey, illness) to train ganying feedback.
4) Cultivation: treat fear at sea/life-edge as a gate for refining xin (sincerity) rather than panic.
5) Record answered/unanswered patterns to refine personal ritual timing with the calendar." , "logic_compare"  : "Unlike abstract female immortal biographies focused on ascent, this text proves sanctity by horizontal rescue across human classes. Unlike pure state hagiography, miracles lead recognition rather than reverse. Distinctive because efficacy under contingency is the epistemic core." } , { "name_han"  : "湄洲屿志略" , "logic_thesis"  : "It proves that place is an argument: Meizhou’s geography, genealogy, and shrine history demonstrate that numinous power is site-anchored and then radiates outward. Local landscape + lineage narrative convert a person into a territorial deity whose authority travels with diaspora. Sacred geography is therefore causal infrastructure for cult and identity." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: deities require a root-place where qi, memory, and ritual condense.
2) Premise: Meizhou’s island setting and family/community history fix Tianfei’s origin body.
3) Inference: gazetteer data (sites, dates, miracles, offices) stabilize the deity’s ‘address’ in cosmos and empire.
4) Inference: pilgrims and migrants carry the place-logic abroad, cloning the root via branch temples.
5) Conclusion: correct worship and legitimacy require orientation to the root-island as axis of transmission." , "logic_practice"  : "1) In BaZi, identify ‘root places’ in the chart (strong Earth branches, home palace, ancestral indicators) as cultivatable bases.
2) When luck cycles pull a person abroad, maintain ritual link to natal root (ancestral/altar) to avoid qi rootlessness.
3) Practice pilgrimage or oriented meditation toward a chosen sacred axis when chart is scattered.
4) Use place-based offerings timed to chart directional years (east/south etc.).
5) For lineage work, stabilize one home altar before multiplying talismans/statues." , "logic_compare"  : "Compared with 天妃显圣录 (miracle anthology), this text proves by topography and institutional memory. Compared with pure myth, it uses gazetteer form to make sanctity cartographic. Why it differs: it treats island geography as the logical ground of the goddess’s portable power." } , { "name_han"  : "白礁志略" , "logic_thesis"  : "It argues that Baijiao as cult center of Baosheng Dadi proves medical-numinous efficacy is territorialized: healing power is stored in place, genealogy, and temple economy, then exported by devotees. Local monographs convert clinical miracle into communal infrastructure. The deity’s authority is thus a public health cosmology rooted in one shore." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: illness is disorder of qi that both medicine and divine response can reorder.
2) Premise: Baosheng’s efficacy is historically concentrated at Baijiao.
3) Inference: gazetteer records of cures, rites, and lineage make the site a reliable node of healing power.
4) Inference: diaspora temples remain valid when oriented to this node.
5) Conclusion: healing devotion is rational when coordinated with place-memory and medical practice, not superstition alone." , "logic_practice"  : "1) In charts with illness indicators, combine medical action with a fixed healing altar/direction rather than random prayer.
2) Use Fire/Earth useful gods (physician-deity resonance) when Baosheng-type cult is chosen as support.
3) Practice: seasonal purification rites at home when health stars are active.
4) Map ‘clinic + temple’ dual path: diagnosis first, then vow—mirroring text’s medical-divine pairing.
5) For cultivators, treat body as local shrine: daily regimen stabilizes ‘Baijiao’ of the self." , "logic_compare"  : "Unlike pure medical classics, it proves healing via sacred geography. Unlike Tianfei sea-rescue texts, the core contingency is disease, not voyage. Distinct because public healing and place monograph fuse into one legitimacy machine." } , { "name_han"  : "慈济宫碑" , "logic_thesis"  : "The stele argues that carved public memory freezes efficacy into institutional truth: miracles, titles, and patronage become permanently citable evidence. Stone text converts fleeting ganying into legal-ritual capital for the temple. Thus inscription is a logic of authentication—writing as solidification of de." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: oral miracles fade and invite dispute.
2) Premise: stele narration selects verified benefits, donors, and imperial/local recognition.
3) Inference: public stone creates shared reference that binds community and state to the cult.
4) Inference: later rites and claims can appeal to the inscription as proof.
5) Conclusion: durable writing is part of the causal chain that maintains divine office in society." , "logic_practice"  : "1) In BaZi counseling, write down key chart conclusions and vows—externalize memory so practice does not drift.
2) Create a personal ‘stele’: a concise useful-god constitution you re-read each luck cycle.
3) When a ritual works, record date/pillar conditions to build authentic personal canon.
4) Cultivation: journal verified mind-body shifts as institutional memory of your path.
5) Prefer fewer stable commitments over many unrecorded experiments." , "logic_compare"  : "Differs from narrative hagiography by using monumental public form; differs from gazetteers by single-focus authentication of one palace. Why: the stele’s logic is juridical permanence—proof that can be pointed to—rather than encyclopedic place survey." } , { "name_han"  : "临水平妖传" , "logic_thesis"  : "It proves that feminine ritual mastery (Chen Jinggu) can order chaos by confronting demons of birth, drought, and social disorder—authority comes from disciplined technique and sacrifice, not only male lineage priesthood. Pacifying yao is shown as public service cosmology: the body of the ritualist becomes the frontier where community safety is won. Maternal and martial powers are not opposites but one office of protection." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: yao/disorder arise where qi, desire, and neglect open gaps in social-cosmic order.
2) Premise: Chen Jinggu’s training yields techniques (exorcism, weather, midwifery rites) that close those gaps.
3) Inference: successful pacification validates female ritual sovereignty in the Southeast cult sphere.
4) Inference: personal cost (self-sacrifice motifs) is the price that converts power into trustworthy office.
5) Conclusion: order is restored when specialized ritual skill meets communal need under ethical severity." , "logic_practice"  : "1) For charts with strong resource/output clash around children/relationship, use protective ritual timing rather than only luck-waiting.
2) Treat ‘demon’ as named pattern (addiction, panic, toxic bond) and apply a specific counter-technique + vow.
3) Cultivate discipline of the body (sleep, purity rules before rites) as Chen’s training analog.
4) In years of Peach Blossom + kill-sha mix, prioritize boundary rites and midwifery-of-projects (careful gestation of plans).
5) Practice compassionate severity: cut chaos early rather than soft indulgence." , "logic_compare"  : "Unlike male-centered thunder-rite novels, it centers a goddess-shaman lineage of protection and birth. Unlike pure temple gazetteers, it uses narrative combat to prove method. Distinctive logic: maternal-martial fusion as the proof of legitimate power." } , { "name_han"  : "海游记" , "logic_thesis"  : "It argues that sea travel is a moral-cosmic trial: crossing water exposes character and activates divine arbitration, so adventure is not entertainment alone but a laboratory of retribution and aid. Encounters at sea prove that human plots remain nested in larger judgment structures. Mobility tests virtue under risk." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: the sea removes ordinary social shields and compresses fate into voyage events.
2) Premise: helpers, spirits, and punishments appear proportionate to conduct and sincerity.
3) Inference: narrative fortunes at sea encode a theodicy of travel.
4) Inference: readers learn risk ethics—greed, loyalty, devotion—as causal levers.
5) Conclusion: to ‘travel the sea’ is to enter a domain where BaZi-like contingency becomes visible as moral physics." , "logic_practice"  : "1) Before long travel luck years, audit ethics of the trip (intent, partners) as part of risk calculus.
2) Strengthen Water-management in the chart via preparation (info, insurance, rites) not bravado.
3) Use journey as cultivation retreat: reduced comfort to reveal habitual qi leaks.
4) Invoke protective deities consistent with chart useful gods when crossing literal/metaphorical seas.
5) Debrief each major trip against pillar activations to refine travel-year strategy." , "logic_compare"  : "Compared with 天妃显圣录, the focus is the traveler’s moral plotline, not only the goddess’s miracle list. Compared with inland xia novels, water is the decisive arena of judgment. Why different: mobility itself is the metaphysical operator." } , { "name_han"  : "古田县临水顺懿庙记" , "logic_thesis"  : "It proves that local administrative-literary recognition transforms a popular mediumistic cult into orthoprax ‘Shunyi’ order: naming, temple record, and elite prose stabilize Chen Jinggu’s office as protectress. The text’s logic is legitimation through inscription of benefits to the county. Folk power becomes civic cosmology." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: local disorder and childbirth/epidemic anxieties need a recognized numinous office.
2) Premise: the Linshui cult demonstrates repeated protection at Gutian.
3) Inference: literati temple-record confers titles and narrative that bind gentry and people.
4) Inference: once recorded, the goddess’s duties become part of local governance of fortune.
5) Conclusion: correct cult is co-authored by efficacy and elite textual ratification." , "logic_practice"  : "1) When a personal practice works, give it a clear name and rule-set (your ‘temple record’).
2) Align private devotion with socially constructive aims (family protection, community calm) to stabilize it.
3) In BaZi, institutionalize useful-god strategy in writing so family members can follow consistently.
4) Use annual festival-like reviews of the chart (like temple anniversary) rather than only crisis prayer.
5) Seek ‘dual ratification’: felt efficacy + reasoned ethical frame." , "logic_compare"  : "Unlike 临水平妖传’s narrative exorcism, this is officializing prose. Unlike pure myth, it is place-administration of the sacred. Difference reason: it shows how a county turns a goddess into infrastructure via commemorative logic." } , { "name_han"  : "凤山寺志略" , "logic_thesis"  : "It argues that mountain-temple gazetteers prove sanctity by continuous historical layering—founding, miracles, repairs, literati visits—so that the temple’s qi is cumulative institutional memory. Fengshan’s legitimacy is the integral of time-on-site, not a single legend. Devotion is thus faithfulness to a durable axis." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: a mountain temple concentrates landscape qi and human intention over centuries.
2) Premise: successive records of response and patronage form a chain of evidence.
3) Inference: the temple’s power is path-dependent; neglect breaks the chain, restoration renews it.
4) Inference: pilgrims plug into an accumulated field, not only an abstract god-name.
5) Conclusion: orthopraxy includes historical maintenance of the site as causal work." , "logic_practice"  : "1) Treat long-term chart cultivation as temple repair: small consistent rites beat rare grand gestures.
2) Identify a lifelong ‘mountain’ in the chart (stable useful god) and keep funding it with behavior.
3) After bad luck periods, do restoration sequences (health, debt, altar cleaning) analogous to temple rebuild.
4) Study personal history layers (decade luck) like gazetteer chapters before predicting next moves.
5) Avoid abandoning a working practice after one silence period; cumulative logic expects gaps." , "logic_compare"  : "Differs from single-miracle pamphlets by multi-generational accounting. Differs from novelistic saint biographies by institutional continuity. Why: cumulative site-history is the proof structure." } , { "name_han"  : "郭山庙志" , "logic_thesis"  : "It proves that a regional protector cult (often linked to Guangze Zunwang type mountain worship in the Minnan sphere) gains authority by mapping kinship, migration, and temple networks onto one mountain axis. The gazetteer’s logic is network legitimacy: branches are valid when they remain oriented to Guo Mountain’s root virtue. Social cohesion is sacralized geography." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: diaspora communities need a portable yet rooted protector.
2) Premise: Guo Mountain temple accumulates miracles, titles, and clan ties.
3) Inference: written temple history standardizes orthopraxy across branches.
4) Inference: identity and mutual aid flow along the cult network as extensions of the mountain’s de.
5) Conclusion: belonging and blessing are co-produced by root-temple orientation and ethical community practice." , "logic_practice"  : "1) For charts of migrants/expats, establish one root devotion/practice to prevent scattered qi.
2) Use family-shared rituals on fixed solar terms as network nodes strengthening collective luck.
3) In BaZi group readings (couples/business), define a common useful-god policy like a temple constitution.
4) Cultivate loyalty and reciprocity as ‘temple network ethics’ that feed back into personal luck.
5) When opening a new venture (branch), ritually reconnect to the original strategy/root chart reading." , "logic_compare"  : "Compared with pure local village gods without diaspora theory, this emphasizes branching without root-loss. Compared with state martyrology, it centers clan-temple continuum. Distinct logic: network geography of blessing." } , { "name_han"  : "清水岩志略" , "logic_thesis"  : "It argues that Qingshui Zushi’s rock-monastery field proves ascetic practice can crystallize into a lasting environmental power that answers drought, illness, and communal crisis. The mountain is both training ground and battery of accumulated cultivation. Thus biography of a monk-saint becomes hydrology and public welfare cosmology." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: intensive cultivation transforms personal qi and, by extension, local response patterns.
2) Premise: Qingshui’s austerities and compassion yield repeated public miracles at the rock.
3) Inference: the site stores and rebroadcasts that power through shrine continuity.
4) Inference: community rites at the rock are rational appeals to a proven field of response.
5) Conclusion: saintly practice is not private escape; it engineers a commons of numinous aid." , "logic_practice"  : "1) Link personal austerity (fasting from excess, digital silence) to concrete vows for family/community benefit.
2) In dry/Metal-Water crisis patterns in BaZi, practice rain-logic analogs: reduce fire-scatter, gather stillness.
3) Choose a fixed practice seat (your ‘rock’) to accumulate field effects.
4) Track health and local life conditions as feedback on whether cultivation is leaking or storing.
5) Prefer long retreats timed to supportive ten-year luck rather than random intensity." , "logic_compare"  : "Unlike pure Chan lamp records focused on mind-to-mind, this ties liberation-work to local material welfare. Unlike thunder-magic novels, proof is monastic endurance plus place. Why different: ascetic accumulation as public infrastructure." } , { "name_han"  : "潮州路明贶三山国王庙记" , "logic_thesis"  : "It proves that the Three Mountain Kings embody a logic of multi-peak sovereignty: plural local mountain powers are federated under one temple office recognized by Yuan-era literati writing. Ethnic-frontier and agrarian protection needs are met by a triad structure rather than a single anthropomorphic emperor-god. Political geography of Lingnan is translated into a theological federalism of peaks." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: Chaozhou’s landscape and populace require protectors matched to multiple mountain domains.
2) Premise: the three kings’ cult shows efficacy in weather, banditry, and communal order.
3) Inference: elite ‘temple record’ integrates folk triad into literate orthodoxy (mingkuang grace).
4) Inference: triad structure models balanced rule—three agencies, one temple constitution.
5) Conclusion: legitimate local theology is federal: plural numina coordinated for public good under recognized grace." , "logic_practice"  : "1) In complex BaZi (multiple competing useful gods), design a triad policy rather than forcing one god only.
2) Assign life domains to distinct agents (career/health/kin) with a unifying code of conduct.
3) Use three-phase rituals across a year (spring raise, summer control, autumn harvest) mirroring multi-peak offices.
4) For team/family charts, federate strengths instead of crowning one member’s element always.
5) When luck shifts, rebalance the triad weights rather than total conversion of strategy." , "logic_compare"  : "Differs from single-patriarch temple records by explicit triadic sovereignty. Differs from national pantheon novels by remaining regional-mountain federalism. Why: landscape plurality forces theological plurality under one grant of ‘bright grace’." } , { "name_han"  : "飞剑记" , "logic_thesis"  : "It argues that the flying sword is externalized will refined to a law-enforcing instrument: immortal justice operates by precise, directed force rather than vague blessing. Lü-type sword lore proves that cultivation must produce a cutting function against evil and delusion. Power without aim is incomplete; aim without refined qi cannot fly." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: the world contains injustices and demons that ignore soft virtue alone.
2) Premise: sword-immortal practice refines qi into a projective, obedient weapon.
3) Inference: miracles of the sword demonstrate mind–qi–instrument unity.
4) Inference: moral discrimination (what to cut) is as necessary as technique.
5) Conclusion: true attainment is measured by clean, timely severance of harm—internally and externally." , "logic_practice"  : "1) In BaZi, identify the ‘sword’ useful god that must cut (often output/power) and train decisive action windows.
2) Daily: one clean cut of a habit (speech, drinking, doomscroll) as flying-sword drill.
3) Use clash years not only as fear but as authorized cutting of dead relationships/projects.
4) Meditation: visualize exhalation as sword return—extend, strike delusion, retrieve to dantian.
5) Never cultivate intensity without ethical targeting rules." , "logic_compare"  : "Unlike pure alchemical quietist texts, it valorizes operative force. Unlike martial hero novels, the sword answers to immortal law and inner refinement. Distinctive proof: projective instrument as the logic of perfected will." } , { "name_han"  : "铁树记" , "logic_thesis"  : "It proves that Xu Xun’s Dao is long-horizon demon-suppression: evil returns in cycles, so true sagehood plants an ‘iron tree’ standard—discipline so firm that future chaos can be judged and cut again. Cultivation is civilizational maintenance, not one-time victory. Lineage transmission is the iron tree that flowers on schedule." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: demonic disorder is recurrent, tied to moral-political decay cycles.
2) Premise: Xu Xun’s conquest establishes methods and a timed prophecy of return.
3) Inference: the iron tree symbolizes non-rotting standards and deferred verification of the Way.
4) Inference: disciples and institutions must hold the method across centuries.
5) Conclusion: legitimacy of a Dao is durability under cyclical test, not only present marvels." , "logic_practice"  : "1) Build BaZi strategies that assume problem recurrence every luck cycle; write contingency protocols.
2) Plant ‘iron tree’ habits that survive mood and fashion (sleep, integrity, basic rite).
3) In chart, track repeating clash patterns across decades as scheduled demon returns.
4) Lineage practice: teach one method to family/students so the cure outlives you.
5) Evaluate teachers by whether their method still works in the next twelve-year phase." , "logic_compare"  : "Compared with single-quest hagiographies, it emphasizes cyclical re-emergence of evil and institutional readiness. Compared with 飞剑记’s immediate sword justice, iron-tree logic is temporal engineering. Why: time-proofing the Dao is the core argument." } , { "name_han"  : "咒枣记" , "logic_thesis"  : "It argues that Sa Shoujian’s jujube-spell economy proves high Dao can inhabit low, portable technique: a humble fruit becomes a vehicle of healing, exorcism, and moral testing. Accessibility does not dilute power when mantra, virtue, and timing cohere. The text legitimizes popular thunder-rite Daoism through narrative of compassionate magic." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: ordinary people cannot access elite alchemy yet suffer real affliction.
2) Premise: spelled jujubes encode mantra + intent + material medium.
3) Inference: repeated healings show that condensed technique can carry cosmic force.
4) Inference: the adept’s virtue polices against commodified abuse of spells.
5) Conclusion: true popular Daoism is portable efficacy under ethical constraint." , "logic_practice"  : "1) Design small, repeatable BaZi remedies (date-specific micro-acts) instead of only grand rituals.
2) Use a single material anchor (tea, rice, talisman paper) to focus intent—your ‘jujube’.
3) In illness-related pillar activations, pair medical care with short mantra-breath protocols.
4) Test techniques for portability under stress travel years.
5) Audit motive each time you use a ‘spell-like’ method; refuse gain that harms." , "logic_compare"  : "Differs from grand cosmic battles in 铁树记 by micro-technique compassion. Differs from purely meditative neidan texts by affirming material spellcraft. Why: the argument is democratization of force without loss of ethical rigor." } , { "name_han"  : "五顯靈官大帝華光天王傳" , "logic_thesis"  : "It proves that Huaguang’s multiple rebirths and fiery office demonstrate identity as a karmic career across forms: divinity is earned through successive rectifications of violence into dharma-protecting fire. The Five Manifestations logic shows power must be repeatedly moralized before it becomes legitimate lingguan authority. Wrath is refined into lawful numen." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: raw spiritual force without ethics produces havoc (fire as uncontrolled).
2) Premise: successive lives/trials re-educate that force toward protecting the Dharma and people.
3) Inference: titles (Lingguan, Huaguang) mark stages of successfully bound wrath.
4) Inference: cult efficacy against evil depends on this converted fire, not on denying fire.
5) Conclusion: legitimate martial divinity is sublimated violence under vow and law." , "logic_practice"  : "1) In charts with strong Fire/Rob Wealth/Seven Killings, aim to employ, not extinguish, the heat.
2) Create vow-constraints for anger: when fire rises, convert to protective action for dependents.
3) Use rebirth logic for luck cycles: each decade is a ‘new incarnation’ to re-train the same flaw.
4) Ritual: candle/fire offerings paired with confession of misuse of power.
5) Career counsel: channel martial energy into law, security, surgery, reform—not pure conflict." , "logic_compare"  : "Unlike pure Buddhist jataka calm, it keeps theater of fire and battle. Unlike static god-lists, identity is multi-life career. Distinctive: conversion of chaotic fire into office is the proof structure." } , { "name_han"  : "韓湘子全傳" , "logic_thesis"  : "It argues that kinship is the hardest barrier and highest proof of the Dao: Han Xiangzi’s mission to convert Han Yu shows transcendence must return as filial-salvific skill, not abandon the world. Immortality that cannot transform the resistant family is incomplete. The novel makes household resistance a philosophical test of true attainment." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: Confucian family duty and Daoist transcendence appear to conflict.
2) Premise: Xiangzi’s miracles aim at converting a paradigmatic Confucian elder.
3) Inference: spectacle is instrumental to teaching, not an end; the target is mind-change in kin.
4) Inference: success would reconcile two value systems under a higher life-and-death truth.
5) Conclusion: authentic cultivation proves itself in the intimate theater of family, not only mountain solitude." , "logic_practice"  : "1) In BaZi with heavy parallel/resource kin signs, design cultivation that includes family care duties.
2) Do not use ‘Dao’ to flee relational debt; schedule repair conversations in supportive month pillars.
3) Use gentle demonstration (changed habits, stable mood) as your ‘miracle’ before doctrines.
4) When facing stubborn elders, practice long-horizon teaching like Xiangzi—multiple approaches across years.
5) Measure progress by reduced family harm patterns, not only personal mystical states." , "logic_compare"  : "Differs from solitary immortal biographies by centering conversion of a famous Confucian relative. Differs from 綠野仙蹤’s broader social canvas by the single kin-axis ordeal. Why: family is the logical crucible where Dao must show public truth." } , { "name_han"  : "綠野仙蹤" , "logic_thesis"  : "It proves a synthetic thesis: immortality training, political chaos, and popular ethics intertwine so that neidan, magic, and historical turmoil form one causal field. Escape to the mountains is insufficient; the adept must navigate wealth, sex, bureaucracy, and rebellion without losing the embryo of the Dao. The novel argues for engaged transcendence under Qing narrative realism." , "logic_chain"  : "1) Premise: late-imperial society presents total temptations that break half-cooked cultivators.
2) Premise: protagonists pursue internal alchemy while entangled in wars, swindles, and offices.
3) Inference: only methods that survive social heat are real; pure retreat is untested.
4) Inference: comic and grotesque episodes function as stress tests of virtue and technique.
5) Conclusion: the Way is verified in green wilds and dusty courts alike—wholeness under contradiction." , "logic_practice"  : "1) Train BaZi strategy that works in messy careers, not only in ideal ‘mountain’ years.
2) Stress-test cultivation during peak Peach Blossom, wealth, and power activations.
3) Keep a dual ledger: spiritual metrics and worldly integrity metrics.
4) Use fiction-like self-review: which subplot (money/sex/status) currently captures your yuanqi?

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument is that the anomalous is not noise but evidence of patterned qi-response: prodigies, dreams, and local cults prove Heaven–Earth–human correspondence operates through omen-logic rather than pure moral sermon. It establishes a taxonomy of the strange so that causality can be read from irregular events, not only from classics. Thus miscellany becomes a method of induction for cosmotechnical judgment.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: all beings and events are permutations of qi under yin–yang/Five Phases.
2) Premises of experience: anomalies (yao, guai, dreams, crafts, local gods) repeatedly co-occur with human action and seasonal/space conditions.
3) Inference: if co-occurrence is stable, anomalies are readable signs, not random marvels.
4) Inference: classification of the strange yields rules of resonance (ganying) usable beyond court historiography.
5) Conclusion: correct knowledge of fate and ritual requires collecting and sorting liminal cases as data for correspondence reasoning.
entries.logic_practice:
1) In BaZi, treat ‘strange’ chart features (extreme imbalance, void, clash clusters) as omen-data, not discard as noise.
2) Build a personal case-file of life events ↔ pillar combinations to induce personal ganying patterns.
3) When a year/month brings anomalous signs, map them to the chart’s active agents before moralizing.
4) For cultivation, use night dreams and body omens as feedback on qi practice rather than superstition to suppress.
5) Prefer multi-source evidence (calendar + body + locale) over single classic quotation.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike systematic Daoist canons (e.g. Baopuzi) that argue from doctrine downward, Youyang Zazu argues from curated anomaly upward. Unlike pure zhiguai entertainment, it implies an empirical archive for correspondence. Its edge is inductive classification of the uncanny as a logic tool for reading fate.

entries.name_han: 新镌京版工师雕斫正式鲁班经匠家镜
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that craft geometry is applied cosmotechnics: correct measure, orientation, and ritual timing convert raw material into a vessel that hosts auspicious qi and repels sha. Carpentry is not mere technique but a micro-ritual of Heaven–Earth alignment. Error in proportion or rite is therefore structural misfortune, not aesthetic failure.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: buildings/tools mediate human dwelling within directional qi fields.
2) Premise: Lu Ban tradition encodes proportions, axes, and taboo days as transmission of cosmic order.
3) Inference: form that matches cosmic measure concentrates shengqi; form that violates it generates sha.
4) Inference: ritual inauguration (offerings, taboo avoidance) seals the geometric work as a living vessel.
5) Conclusion: mastery of craft is inseparable from calendar, direction, and propitiation—technique without rite is incomplete causality.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Align chart ‘structure’ metaphors with house/tool: Day Master as center, supporting stems as load-bearing axes.
2) When advising fengshui/BaZi lifestyle, prioritize orientation and taboo timing over decorative fixes.
3) Treat ‘broken structure’ in BaZi (severe clash/combination damage) as needing reconstruction sequence, not only luck charms.
4) Cultivation analog: regulate body-as-house—breath, posture, schedule—as measured craft under seasonal rules.
5) Use craft-taboo logic for choosing start dates of projects from the natal chart’s useful gods.
entries.logic_compare: Differs from pure fengshui manuals by rooting spatial logic in artisan process and tool-making, not only landscape form. Differs from philosophical Daoism by proving cosmology through buildable measure. Why: it makes the abstract axis of Heaven–Earth into a workshop protocol.

entries.logic_thesis: It argues that maritime salvation by Tianfei is evidence of virtue-power (de) becoming operational force across space: sincere distress plus correct invocation activates a responsive numen. Empire, merchants, and fishers are equalized under one rescue logic—authority of the goddess is proven by repeatable miracle pattern, not by bloodline. Thus cult legitimacy is empirical ganying under crisis.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: the sea is a realm of extreme contingency where human skill is insufficient.
2) Premise: repeated rescues follow prayer, moral sincerity, and recognition of Tianfei’s titles.
3) Inference: efficacy clusters around invocation + de, proving responsive presence.
4) Inference: state and local recognition follow efficacy, so cult grows by verified response, not only decree.
5) Conclusion: the goddess’s ‘logic’ is crisis–sincerity–response; devotion is rational risk-management under cosmically ordered mercy.
entries.logic_practice:
1) In BaZi crisis years (travel, water elements extreme, danger stars), prioritize sincere vow-ritual over fatalist resignation.
2) Map ‘rescue’ deities to chart useful gods: when Water is both danger and resource, cultivate responsive devotion + skill.
3) Practice: short, specific petitions tied to concrete dangers (journey, illness) to train ganying feedback.
4) Cultivation: treat fear at sea/life-edge as a gate for refining xin (sincerity) rather than panic.
5) Record answered/unanswered patterns to refine personal ritual timing with the calendar.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike abstract female immortal biographies focused on ascent, this text proves sanctity by horizontal rescue across human classes. Unlike pure state hagiography, miracles lead recognition rather than reverse. Distinctive because efficacy under contingency is the epistemic core.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that place is an argument: Meizhou’s geography, genealogy, and shrine history demonstrate that numinous power is site-anchored and then radiates outward. Local landscape + lineage narrative convert a person into a territorial deity whose authority travels with diaspora. Sacred geography is therefore causal infrastructure for cult and identity.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: deities require a root-place where qi, memory, and ritual condense.
2) Premise: Meizhou’s island setting and family/community history fix Tianfei’s origin body.
3) Inference: gazetteer data (sites, dates, miracles, offices) stabilize the deity’s ‘address’ in cosmos and empire.
4) Inference: pilgrims and migrants carry the place-logic abroad, cloning the root via branch temples.
5) Conclusion: correct worship and legitimacy require orientation to the root-island as axis of transmission.
entries.logic_practice:
1) In BaZi, identify ‘root places’ in the chart (strong Earth branches, home palace, ancestral indicators) as cultivatable bases.
2) When luck cycles pull a person abroad, maintain ritual link to natal root (ancestral/altar) to avoid qi rootlessness.
3) Practice pilgrimage or oriented meditation toward a chosen sacred axis when chart is scattered.
4) Use place-based offerings timed to chart directional years (east/south etc.).
5) For lineage work, stabilize one home altar before multiplying talismans/statues.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 天妃显圣录 (miracle anthology), this text proves by topography and institutional memory. Compared with pure myth, it uses gazetteer form to make sanctity cartographic. Why it differs: it treats island geography as the logical ground of the goddess’s portable power.

entries.logic_thesis: It argues that Baijiao as cult center of Baosheng Dadi proves medical-numinous efficacy is territorialized: healing power is stored in place, genealogy, and temple economy, then exported by devotees. Local monographs convert clinical miracle into communal infrastructure. The deity’s authority is thus a public health cosmology rooted in one shore.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: illness is disorder of qi that both medicine and divine response can reorder.
2) Premise: Baosheng’s efficacy is historically concentrated at Baijiao.
3) Inference: gazetteer records of cures, rites, and lineage make the site a reliable node of healing power.
4) Inference: diaspora temples remain valid when oriented to this node.
5) Conclusion: healing devotion is rational when coordinated with place-memory and medical practice, not superstition alone.
entries.logic_practice:
1) In charts with illness indicators, combine medical action with a fixed healing altar/direction rather than random prayer.
2) Use Fire/Earth useful gods (physician-deity resonance) when Baosheng-type cult is chosen as support.
3) Practice: seasonal purification rites at home when health stars are active.
4) Map ‘clinic + temple’ dual path: diagnosis first, then vow—mirroring text’s medical-divine pairing.
5) For cultivators, treat body as local shrine: daily regimen stabilizes ‘Baijiao’ of the self.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure medical classics, it proves healing via sacred geography. Unlike Tianfei sea-rescue texts, the core contingency is disease, not voyage. Distinct because public healing and place monograph fuse into one legitimacy machine.

entries.logic_thesis: The stele argues that carved public memory freezes efficacy into institutional truth: miracles, titles, and patronage become permanently citable evidence. Stone text converts fleeting ganying into legal-ritual capital for the temple. Thus inscription is a logic of authentication—writing as solidification of de.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: oral miracles fade and invite dispute.
2) Premise: stele narration selects verified benefits, donors, and imperial/local recognition.
3) Inference: public stone creates shared reference that binds community and state to the cult.
4) Inference: later rites and claims can appeal to the inscription as proof.
5) Conclusion: durable writing is part of the causal chain that maintains divine office in society.
entries.logic_practice:
1) In BaZi counseling, write down key chart conclusions and vows—externalize memory so practice does not drift.
2) Create a personal ‘stele’: a concise useful-god constitution you re-read each luck cycle.
3) When a ritual works, record date/pillar conditions to build authentic personal canon.
4) Cultivation: journal verified mind-body shifts as institutional memory of your path.
5) Prefer fewer stable commitments over many unrecorded experiments.
entries.logic_compare: Differs from narrative hagiography by using monumental public form; differs from gazetteers by single-focus authentication of one palace. Why: the stele’s logic is juridical permanence—proof that can be pointed to—rather than encyclopedic place survey.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that feminine ritual mastery (Chen Jinggu) can order chaos by confronting demons of birth, drought, and social disorder—authority comes from disciplined technique and sacrifice, not only male lineage priesthood. Pacifying yao is shown as public service cosmology: the body of the ritualist becomes the frontier where community safety is won. Maternal and martial powers are not opposites but one office of protection.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: yao/disorder arise where qi, desire, and neglect open gaps in social-cosmic order.
2) Premise: Chen Jinggu’s training yields techniques (exorcism, weather, midwifery rites) that close those gaps.
3) Inference: successful pacification validates female ritual sovereignty in the Southeast cult sphere.
4) Inference: personal cost (self-sacrifice motifs) is the price that converts power into trustworthy office.
5) Conclusion: order is restored when specialized ritual skill meets communal need under ethical severity.
entries.logic_practice:
1) For charts with strong resource/output clash around children/relationship, use protective ritual timing rather than only luck-waiting.
2) Treat ‘demon’ as named pattern (addiction, panic, toxic bond) and apply a specific counter-technique + vow.
3) Cultivate discipline of the body (sleep, purity rules before rites) as Chen’s training analog.
4) In years of Peach Blossom + kill-sha mix, prioritize boundary rites and midwifery-of-projects (careful gestation of plans).
5) Practice compassionate severity: cut chaos early rather than soft indulgence.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike male-centered thunder-rite novels, it centers a goddess-shaman lineage of protection and birth. Unlike pure temple gazetteers, it uses narrative combat to prove method. Distinctive logic: maternal-martial fusion as the proof of legitimate power.

entries.logic_thesis: It argues that sea travel is a moral-cosmic trial: crossing water exposes character and activates divine arbitration, so adventure is not entertainment alone but a laboratory of retribution and aid. Encounters at sea prove that human plots remain nested in larger judgment structures. Mobility tests virtue under risk.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: the sea removes ordinary social shields and compresses fate into voyage events.
2) Premise: helpers, spirits, and punishments appear proportionate to conduct and sincerity.
3) Inference: narrative fortunes at sea encode a theodicy of travel.
4) Inference: readers learn risk ethics—greed, loyalty, devotion—as causal levers.
5) Conclusion: to ‘travel the sea’ is to enter a domain where BaZi-like contingency becomes visible as moral physics.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Before long travel luck years, audit ethics of the trip (intent, partners) as part of risk calculus.
2) Strengthen Water-management in the chart via preparation (info, insurance, rites) not bravado.
3) Use journey as cultivation retreat: reduced comfort to reveal habitual qi leaks.
4) Invoke protective deities consistent with chart useful gods when crossing literal/metaphorical seas.
5) Debrief each major trip against pillar activations to refine travel-year strategy.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 天妃显圣录, the focus is the traveler’s moral plotline, not only the goddess’s miracle list. Compared with inland xia novels, water is the decisive arena of judgment. Why different: mobility itself is the metaphysical operator.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that local administrative-literary recognition transforms a popular mediumistic cult into orthoprax ‘Shunyi’ order: naming, temple record, and elite prose stabilize Chen Jinggu’s office as protectress. The text’s logic is legitimation through inscription of benefits to the county. Folk power becomes civic cosmology.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: local disorder and childbirth/epidemic anxieties need a recognized numinous office.
2) Premise: the Linshui cult demonstrates repeated protection at Gutian.
3) Inference: literati temple-record confers titles and narrative that bind gentry and people.
4) Inference: once recorded, the goddess’s duties become part of local governance of fortune.
5) Conclusion: correct cult is co-authored by efficacy and elite textual ratification.
entries.logic_practice:
1) When a personal practice works, give it a clear name and rule-set (your ‘temple record’).
2) Align private devotion with socially constructive aims (family protection, community calm) to stabilize it.
3) In BaZi, institutionalize useful-god strategy in writing so family members can follow consistently.
4) Use annual festival-like reviews of the chart (like temple anniversary) rather than only crisis prayer.
5) Seek ‘dual ratification’: felt efficacy + reasoned ethical frame.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 临水平妖传’s narrative exorcism, this is officializing prose. Unlike pure myth, it is place-administration of the sacred. Difference reason: it shows how a county turns a goddess into infrastructure via commemorative logic.

entries.logic_thesis: It argues that mountain-temple gazetteers prove sanctity by continuous historical layering—founding, miracles, repairs, literati visits—so that the temple’s qi is cumulative institutional memory. Fengshan’s legitimacy is the integral of time-on-site, not a single legend. Devotion is thus faithfulness to a durable axis.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: a mountain temple concentrates landscape qi and human intention over centuries.
2) Premise: successive records of response and patronage form a chain of evidence.
3) Inference: the temple’s power is path-dependent; neglect breaks the chain, restoration renews it.
4) Inference: pilgrims plug into an accumulated field, not only an abstract god-name.
5) Conclusion: orthopraxy includes historical maintenance of the site as causal work.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Treat long-term chart cultivation as temple repair: small consistent rites beat rare grand gestures.
2) Identify a lifelong ‘mountain’ in the chart (stable useful god) and keep funding it with behavior.
3) After bad luck periods, do restoration sequences (health, debt, altar cleaning) analogous to temple rebuild.
4) Study personal history layers (decade luck) like gazetteer chapters before predicting next moves.
5) Avoid abandoning a working practice after one silence period; cumulative logic expects gaps.
entries.logic_compare: Differs from single-miracle pamphlets by multi-generational accounting. Differs from novelistic saint biographies by institutional continuity. Why: cumulative site-history is the proof structure.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that a regional protector cult (often linked to Guangze Zunwang type mountain worship in the Minnan sphere) gains authority by mapping kinship, migration, and temple networks onto one mountain axis. The gazetteer’s logic is network legitimacy: branches are valid when they remain oriented to Guo Mountain’s root virtue. Social cohesion is sacralized geography.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: diaspora communities need a portable yet rooted protector.
2) Premise: Guo Mountain temple accumulates miracles, titles, and clan ties.
3) Inference: written temple history standardizes orthopraxy across branches.
4) Inference: identity and mutual aid flow along the cult network as extensions of the mountain’s de.
5) Conclusion: belonging and blessing are co-produced by root-temple orientation and ethical community practice.
entries.logic_practice:
1) For charts of migrants/expats, establish one root devotion/practice to prevent scattered qi.
2) Use family-shared rituals on fixed solar terms as network nodes strengthening collective luck.
3) In BaZi group readings (couples/business), define a common useful-god policy like a temple constitution.
4) Cultivate loyalty and reciprocity as ‘temple network ethics’ that feed back into personal luck.
5) When opening a new venture (branch), ritually reconnect to the original strategy/root chart reading.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with pure local village gods without diaspora theory, this emphasizes branching without root-loss. Compared with state martyrology, it centers clan-temple continuum. Distinct logic: network geography of blessing.

entries.logic_thesis: It argues that Qingshui Zushi’s rock-monastery field proves ascetic practice can crystallize into a lasting environmental power that answers drought, illness, and communal crisis. The mountain is both training ground and battery of accumulated cultivation. Thus biography of a monk-saint becomes hydrology and public welfare cosmology.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: intensive cultivation transforms personal qi and, by extension, local response patterns.
2) Premise: Qingshui’s austerities and compassion yield repeated public miracles at the rock.
3) Inference: the site stores and rebroadcasts that power through shrine continuity.
4) Inference: community rites at the rock are rational appeals to a proven field of response.
5) Conclusion: saintly practice is not private escape; it engineers a commons of numinous aid.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Link personal austerity (fasting from excess, digital silence) to concrete vows for family/community benefit.
2) In dry/Metal-Water crisis patterns in BaZi, practice rain-logic analogs: reduce fire-scatter, gather stillness.
3) Choose a fixed practice seat (your ‘rock’) to accumulate field effects.
4) Track health and local life conditions as feedback on whether cultivation is leaking or storing.
5) Prefer long retreats timed to supportive ten-year luck rather than random intensity.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure Chan lamp records focused on mind-to-mind, this ties liberation-work to local material welfare. Unlike thunder-magic novels, proof is monastic endurance plus place. Why different: ascetic accumulation as public infrastructure.

entries.name_han: 潮州路明贶三山国王庙记
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the Three Mountain Kings embody a logic of multi-peak sovereignty: plural local mountain powers are federated under one temple office recognized by Yuan-era literati writing. Ethnic-frontier and agrarian protection needs are met by a triad structure rather than a single anthropomorphic emperor-god. Political geography of Lingnan is translated into a theological federalism of peaks.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: Chaozhou’s landscape and populace require protectors matched to multiple mountain domains.
2) Premise: the three kings’ cult shows efficacy in weather, banditry, and communal order.
3) Inference: elite ‘temple record’ integrates folk triad into literate orthodoxy (mingkuang grace).
4) Inference: triad structure models balanced rule—three agencies, one temple constitution.
5) Conclusion: legitimate local theology is federal: plural numina coordinated for public good under recognized grace.
entries.logic_practice:
1) In complex BaZi (multiple competing useful gods), design a triad policy rather than forcing one god only.
2) Assign life domains to distinct agents (career/health/kin) with a unifying code of conduct.
3) Use three-phase rituals across a year (spring raise, summer control, autumn harvest) mirroring multi-peak offices.
4) For team/family charts, federate strengths instead of crowning one member’s element always.
5) When luck shifts, rebalance the triad weights rather than total conversion of strategy.
entries.logic_compare: Differs from single-patriarch temple records by explicit triadic sovereignty. Differs from national pantheon novels by remaining regional-mountain federalism. Why: landscape plurality forces theological plurality under one grant of ‘bright grace’.

entries.logic_thesis: It argues that the flying sword is externalized will refined to a law-enforcing instrument: immortal justice operates by precise, directed force rather than vague blessing. Lü-type sword lore proves that cultivation must produce a cutting function against evil and delusion. Power without aim is incomplete; aim without refined qi cannot fly.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: the world contains injustices and demons that ignore soft virtue alone.
2) Premise: sword-immortal practice refines qi into a projective, obedient weapon.
3) Inference: miracles of the sword demonstrate mind–qi–instrument unity.
4) Inference: moral discrimination (what to cut) is as necessary as technique.
5) Conclusion: true attainment is measured by clean, timely severance of harm—internally and externally.
entries.logic_practice:
1) In BaZi, identify the ‘sword’ useful god that must cut (often output/power) and train decisive action windows.
2) Daily: one clean cut of a habit (speech, drinking, doomscroll) as flying-sword drill.
3) Use clash years not only as fear but as authorized cutting of dead relationships/projects.
4) Meditation: visualize exhalation as sword return—extend, strike delusion, retrieve to dantian.
5) Never cultivate intensity without ethical targeting rules.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure alchemical quietist texts, it valorizes operative force. Unlike martial hero novels, the sword answers to immortal law and inner refinement. Distinctive proof: projective instrument as the logic of perfected will.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that Xu Xun’s Dao is long-horizon demon-suppression: evil returns in cycles, so true sagehood plants an ‘iron tree’ standard—discipline so firm that future chaos can be judged and cut again. Cultivation is civilizational maintenance, not one-time victory. Lineage transmission is the iron tree that flowers on schedule.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: demonic disorder is recurrent, tied to moral-political decay cycles.
2) Premise: Xu Xun’s conquest establishes methods and a timed prophecy of return.
3) Inference: the iron tree symbolizes non-rotting standards and deferred verification of the Way.
4) Inference: disciples and institutions must hold the method across centuries.
5) Conclusion: legitimacy of a Dao is durability under cyclical test, not only present marvels.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Build BaZi strategies that assume problem recurrence every luck cycle; write contingency protocols.
2) Plant ‘iron tree’ habits that survive mood and fashion (sleep, integrity, basic rite).
3) In chart, track repeating clash patterns across decades as scheduled demon returns.
4) Lineage practice: teach one method to family/students so the cure outlives you.
5) Evaluate teachers by whether their method still works in the next twelve-year phase.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with single-quest hagiographies, it emphasizes cyclical re-emergence of evil and institutional readiness. Compared with 飞剑记’s immediate sword justice, iron-tree logic is temporal engineering. Why: time-proofing the Dao is the core argument.

entries.logic_thesis: It argues that Sa Shoujian’s jujube-spell economy proves high Dao can inhabit low, portable technique: a humble fruit becomes a vehicle of healing, exorcism, and moral testing. Accessibility does not dilute power when mantra, virtue, and timing cohere. The text legitimizes popular thunder-rite Daoism through narrative of compassionate magic.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: ordinary people cannot access elite alchemy yet suffer real affliction.
2) Premise: spelled jujubes encode mantra + intent + material medium.
3) Inference: repeated healings show that condensed technique can carry cosmic force.
4) Inference: the adept’s virtue polices against commodified abuse of spells.
5) Conclusion: true popular Daoism is portable efficacy under ethical constraint.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Design small, repeatable BaZi remedies (date-specific micro-acts) instead of only grand rituals.
2) Use a single material anchor (tea, rice, talisman paper) to focus intent—your ‘jujube’.
3) In illness-related pillar activations, pair medical care with short mantra-breath protocols.
4) Test techniques for portability under stress travel years.
5) Audit motive each time you use a ‘spell-like’ method; refuse gain that harms.
entries.logic_compare: Differs from grand cosmic battles in 铁树记 by micro-technique compassion. Differs from purely meditative neidan texts by affirming material spellcraft. Why: the argument is democratization of force without loss of ethical rigor.

entries.name_han: 五顯靈官大帝華光天王傳
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that Huaguang’s multiple rebirths and fiery office demonstrate identity as a karmic career across forms: divinity is earned through successive rectifications of violence into dharma-protecting fire. The Five Manifestations logic shows power must be repeatedly moralized before it becomes legitimate lingguan authority. Wrath is refined into lawful numen.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: raw spiritual force without ethics produces havoc (fire as uncontrolled).
2) Premise: successive lives/trials re-educate that force toward protecting the Dharma and people.
3) Inference: titles (Lingguan, Huaguang) mark stages of successfully bound wrath.
4) Inference: cult efficacy against evil depends on this converted fire, not on denying fire.
5) Conclusion: legitimate martial divinity is sublimated violence under vow and law.
entries.logic_practice:
1) In charts with strong Fire/Rob Wealth/Seven Killings, aim to employ, not extinguish, the heat.
2) Create vow-constraints for anger: when fire rises, convert to protective action for dependents.
3) Use rebirth logic for luck cycles: each decade is a ‘new incarnation’ to re-train the same flaw.
4) Ritual: candle/fire offerings paired with confession of misuse of power.
5) Career counsel: channel martial energy into law, security, surgery, reform—not pure conflict.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure Buddhist jataka calm, it keeps theater of fire and battle. Unlike static god-lists, identity is multi-life career. Distinctive: conversion of chaotic fire into office is the proof structure.

entries.logic_thesis: It argues that kinship is the hardest barrier and highest proof of the Dao: Han Xiangzi’s mission to convert Han Yu shows transcendence must return as filial-salvific skill, not abandon the world. Immortality that cannot transform the resistant family is incomplete. The novel makes household resistance a philosophical test of true attainment.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: Confucian family duty and Daoist transcendence appear to conflict.
2) Premise: Xiangzi’s miracles aim at converting a paradigmatic Confucian elder.
3) Inference: spectacle is instrumental to teaching, not an end; the target is mind-change in kin.
4) Inference: success would reconcile two value systems under a higher life-and-death truth.
5) Conclusion: authentic cultivation proves itself in the intimate theater of family, not only mountain solitude.
entries.logic_practice:
1) In BaZi with heavy parallel/resource kin signs, design cultivation that includes family care duties.
2) Do not use ‘Dao’ to flee relational debt; schedule repair conversations in supportive month pillars.
3) Use gentle demonstration (changed habits, stable mood) as your ‘miracle’ before doctrines.
4) When facing stubborn elders, practice long-horizon teaching like Xiangzi—multiple approaches across years.
5) Measure progress by reduced family harm patterns, not only personal mystical states.
entries.logic_compare: Differs from solitary immortal biographies by centering conversion of a famous Confucian relative. Differs from 綠野仙蹤’s broader social canvas by the single kin-axis ordeal. Why: family is the logical crucible where Dao must show public truth.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves a synthetic thesis: immortality training, political chaos, and popular ethics intertwine so that neidan, magic, and historical turmoil form one causal field. Escape to the mountains is insufficient; the adept must navigate wealth, sex, bureaucracy, and rebellion without losing the embryo of the Dao. The novel argues for engaged transcendence under Qing narrative realism.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: late-imperial society presents total temptations that break half-cooked cultivators.
2) Premise: protagonists pursue internal alchemy while entangled in wars, swindles, and offices.
3) Inference: only methods that survive social heat are real; pure retreat is untested.
4) Inference: comic and grotesque episodes function as stress tests of virtue and technique.
5) Conclusion: the Way is verified in green wilds and dusty courts alike—wholeness under contradiction.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Train BaZi strategy that works in messy careers, not only in ideal ‘mountain’ years.
2) Stress-test cultivation during peak Peach Blossom, wealth, and power activations.
3) Keep a dual ledger: spiritual metrics and worldly integrity metrics.
4) Use fiction-like self-review: which subplot (money/sex/status) currently captures your yuanqi?
5) Schedule alternate phases of retreat and re-entry each luck cycle.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with shorter Shenxian novels (飞剑/铁树/咒枣), it is panoramic and socially dense. Compared with pure neidan manuals, it insists on political-economic trial. Why different: encyclopedic life-world as the only adequate proof of the Dao.

entries.name_han: 北方真武祖師玄天上帝出身志傳
entries.logic_thesis: It argues that Xuantian Shangdi’s origin—from royal/ascetic struggle to northern guardian—proves cosmic order requires a perfected martial-stillness at the north: demons of desire are subdued so that the empire of Heaven has a fixed polar enforcer. Cultivation narrative becomes geopolitics of the sky: the north is not mere direction but the office of final subjugation. Personal renunciation graduates into pantheon policing power.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: ungoverned demons (desire, chaos) threaten both person and cosmos.
2) Premise: the future Zhenwu undergoes severe ascesis and battles to cut those demons.
3) Inference: attainment qualifies him for northern command under higher Daoist gods.
4) Inference: cult of True Warrior is participation in polar ordering of qi (water, winter, stillness-with-sword).
5) Conclusion: the logical end of self-conquest is becoming a stable guardian function in the larger order.
entries.logic_practice:
1) For charts needing northern Water/stillness (overactive Fire/Wind), adopt Zhenwu regimen: early sleep, cold-calm breath, reduced stimulant.
2) Pair stillness with a ‘sword’ rule: one decisive daily cut of a demon-habit.
3) In winter and Water luck, intensify retreat; in Fire years, emphasize demon-naming and restraint.
4) Altar practice facing north when working on willpower and protection.
5) Frame personal discipline as training for service—self-rule for the sake of those you protect.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike purely local southeast goddess gazetteers, this is polar-cosmic office making. Unlike 飞剑记’s wandering sword service, Zhenwu is fixed as northern axis after conquest of self. Why: the thesis is that ultimate cultivation installs a permanent guardian coordinate in the cosmos, not only episodic heroism.
